passage:
Counsellor's note, Class 9.

Gopika was referred by her class teacher after going blank when called on in physics. In our talk she said she freezes as soon as Mr Arnab enters, her hands go cold, and she avoids his eyes. I asked whether he has ever mocked anyone. She thought and said no; he only expects homework done and silence during explanation. We talked about how strict and cruel are different things. Together we made a small plan: revise the day's topic a little longer the night before, and ask him one question a week, written down beforehand. Last Friday she asked about a diagram. Mr Arnab answered plainly and said "good question." She reported that her voice shook but she got the words out. I will check in again after the exam.

qa.q: What small plan did Gopika and the counsellor make?
qa.a: To revise the day's topic a little longer the night before and to ask Mr Arnab one written question a week.

qa.q: What was Gopika feeling when Mr Arnab entered the room, and what shows it?
qa.a: She was scared. Her hands went cold, she avoided his eyes and she froze when he called on her.

qa.q: Why does the counsellor talk with Gopika about strict versus cruel?
qa.a: So she can see that Mr Arnab is demanding but has never mocked anyone, which makes him easier to approach. A teacher who was cruel would call for telling an adult instead.

qa.q: How might Mr Arnab see Gopika's question about the diagram?
qa.a: Likely as a welcome sign of interest. He answered plainly and said "good question", so he seems glad a quiet student spoke up.

grounding: A student afraid of a strict teacher prepares more and asks one question a week, separating strictness from cruelty.

passage:
Mr Tomas taught physics at Xin's international school in Prague, and he was famous for his stare. When he asked a question, the whole room froze. Xin froze most of all. Her mind went white. She'd stopped raising her hand in September.
One evening she talked to her older cousin about it on a video call.
"Is he cruel?" her cousin asked. "Or just strict?"
Xin thought. He never insulted anyone. He just expected answers. "Strict, I guess."
"Then prepare a bit more. And put your hand up once every week. Just one question."
So Xin read the next chapter the night before. On Tuesday, heart pounding, she raised her hand. "Sir, why does the ball fall at the same speed as the feather in the vacuum?"
Mr Tomas's stare turned to her. Then he smiled, just slightly. "Excellent question, Xin."
It wasn't magic. She still felt nervous. But the next week, she asked another.

qa.q: Which city is Xin's international school in?
What was Xin feeling in Mr Tomas's class?
qa.a: She felt frightened and frozen, her mind going white whenever he asked a question.

qa.q: What small steps helped Xin, and why?
qa.a: Preparing a little more and asking one question a week helped her break the ice and see that he was strict, not cruel.

qa.q: How does Mr Tomas seem to see Xin's question?
qa.a: He seems pleased and respectful, smiling slightly and calling it an excellent question.

grounding: A teen scared of a strict teacher prepares more, asks one question a week, and learns to separate strictness from cruelty.

passage:
In the chemistry lab, Sarika ma'am's voice could stop a Bunsen burner. "Goggles on. Now." "Why is that beaker there?" Anjali's hands shook so much she spilled a test tube in the first week, and she hadn't spoken in class since.
At break, her lab partner Neha said, "She's not mean, you know. She's just scared someone will get burnt." Anjali thought about it. Sarika ma'am had never mocked anyone. She'd only been sharp about safety.
That night Anjali read the next practical twice. At the next lab, she raised her hand before starting. "Ma'am, should I add the acid to water or water to acid?"
Sarika ma'am paused. "Acid to water. Always. Good that you asked, Anjali."
Anjali's hands still shook a little. But she finished the practical without spilling a drop, and she decided she'd ask one question every week.

qa.q: What did Anjali spill in the first week?
How did Anjali feel in Sarika ma'am's lab?
qa.a: She felt frightened, her hands shaking, and too scared to speak in class.

qa.q: What helped Anjali overcome her fear?
qa.a: Understanding that Sarika ma'am was strict about safety, not cruel, preparing more and asking one question.

qa.q: How might Sarika ma'am see Anjali's question?
qa.a: She seems to appreciate it, answering clearly and praising Anjali for asking.

grounding: A teen afraid of a strict teacher prepares more, asks a question, and sees strictness is not the same as cruelty.
